page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It runs on dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 processors clocked at 2.8 GHz, comprising 4 physical cores and 8 execution threads via hyperthreading. Hardware resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, 33 MB of shared L3 cache, and 32 GB of system memory (4 GB per vCPU). The CPU supports modern instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512, and AVX-512 VNNI for vectorized execution. The instance contains no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, requiring network-attached persistent disks for all non-volatile storage needs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent average-tier performance across general compute, memory throughput, and network serving workloads. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,464.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 8,292.45, alongside 6,735.0 points in clang software compilation. Memory bandwidth reaches 50.27 GB/s for large uncached reads and 37.18 GB/s for writes. In transactional and serving workloads, the system sustained 7.12 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.9 GB/s in static web serving throughput. However, throughput is comparatively weak in single-threaded gzip compression (23.82 GB/s), ray tracing, and small-model LLM prompt processing (340.65 tokens/sec).

From an architectural standpoint, the n2-standard-8 provides dedicated CPU allocation, avoiding the performance variability associated with shared-core burstable instances. Because it lacks integrated NVMe disks and specialized accelerators, it offers predictable resource density without unneeded hardware overhead. It is well suited for general-purpose application workloads, including microservice backends, static web servers, CI/CD build environments, Redis caching instances, and mid-sized relational database deployments.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Driven by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz across 4 physical cores and 8 execution threads, the instance features 33 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and VNNI instruction sets. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, relying on network storage solutions. In benchmark testing, the n2-standard-8 registers middle-tier results across multi-core computing, software compilation, and in-memory key-value operations, achieving 7.12 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.9 GB/s static web serving throughput. Conversely, intensive compression tasks and small-model LLM prompt processing exhibit weaker relative throughput. This profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-effective for general enterprise workloads, web application serving, CI/CD compilation, and mid-tier databases requiring dedicated compute.
